g1.label: 1 — eight to ten hours of ___
g1.why: Doctors recommend eight to ten hours of sleep a night for teenagers.

g2.label: 2 — blue light tells the ___
g2.why: Blue light sends the wrong signal to the brain, which decides when you feel tired.

g3.label: 3 — a quick ___ between lessons
g3.why: A snack is a small, quick thing to eat between meals.

g4.label: 4 — sugar and ___
g4.why: Energy drinks contain sugar and caffeine, the same stimulant as in coffee.

g5.label: 5 — they can ___ better
g5.why: To concentrate means to keep your attention on something.

g6.label: 6 — thirty minutes of ___
g6.why: Exercise is physical activity; thirty minutes a day is the recommendation.

g7.label: 7 — hormones improve your ___
g7.why: Sport produces hormones that make you feel better — they improve your mood.

g8.label: 8 — good for your mental ___
g8.why: "Mental health" is the fixed phrase for how you feel psychologically.

g1.label: 1 — if you ___ more water
g1.why: In the if-part of a type I sentence you use the present simple, never will.

g2.label: 2 — she ___ so tired tomorrow
g2.why: The main clause of a type I sentence takes will / won't + infinitive.

g3.label: 3 — if you ___ your phone off
g3.why: After if you use the present simple, even when you mean the future.

g4.label: 4 — if we ___ to school
g4.why: The if-clause takes the present simple: if we cycle.

g5.label: 5 — he ___ sleep tonight
g5.why: The result of a real possibility is expressed with will / won't.

g6.label: 6 — if it ___ tomorrow
g6.why: After if you need the present simple, third person singular: rains.

g7.label: 7 — if you ___ them in the kitchen
g7.why: The if-clause takes the present simple: if you help them.

g8.label: 8 — if I ___ time after school
g8.why: After if you use the present simple; the will is already in "I'll come".

g1.label: 1 — if I ___ more free time
g1.why: Type II uses the simple past in the if-clause: if I had more time.

g2.label: 2 — she ___ so tired
g2.why: The main clause of a type II sentence takes would / wouldn't + infinitive.

g3.label: 3 — if you ___ a personal trainer
g3.why: "What would you do if...?" needs the simple past in the if-clause.

g4.label: 4 — if we ___ a swimming pool
g4.why: The if-clause of a type II sentence takes the simple past, not would.

g5.label: 5 — if he ___ less television
g5.why: After if you use the simple past: if he watched less television.

g6.label: 6 — if I ___ you
g6.why: In "If I were you" English uses were, not was, for imagined situations.

g7.label: 7 — if everybody ___ the rules
g7.why: The if-clause takes the simple past — never "would" in the if-part.

g8.label: 8 — she ___ much more energy
g8.why: The main clause of a type II sentence takes would + infinitive.
